# 1 Maccabees Chapter 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_007_page_001.jpg

---

1. In the one hundred and fifty-first year, Demetrius son of Seleucus escaped from Rome, came with a few men to a coastal city, and seized the throne there.
2. As he was entering the royal palace of his ancestors, the troops seized Antiochus and Lysias to hand them over to him.
3. When this was reported to him he said: "Do not let me see their faces."
4. So the troops killed them, and Demetrius took his seat on the throne.
5. Then all the lawless and ungodly men of Israel came to him, led by Alcimus, who wanted to be high priest.
6. They laid charges against the people before the king, saying: "Judas and his brothers have destroyed all your friends and driven us out of our own land.
7. Now therefore send someone you trust to go and see all the destruction Judas has brought upon us and upon the king's territory, and to punish him and all who support him."
8. The king chose Bacchides, one of the king's Friends who governed the Great Plain — a great man, faithful to the king — and sent him.
9. He also sent with him the ungodly Alcimus, to whom he confirmed the high priesthood, and ordered him to exact vengeance on the Israelites.
10. They set out and advanced with a large force into the land of Judah. Bacchides sent messengers to Judas and his brothers with deceptively peaceful words.
11. But they paid no attention, for they saw that he had come with a large force.
12. Then a company of scribes came together to Alcimus and Bacchides to negotiate a just settlement.
13. The Hasideans were the first among the Israelites to seek peace with them; for they said: "A priest of the line of Aaron has come with the army, and he will not do us wrong."
14. Alcimus spoke peaceful words to them and swore an oath: "We will not seek to harm you or your friends."
15. They trusted him; but he seized sixty of them and killed them in a single day, in accordance with the scripture that says:
16. "The flesh of your faithful ones and their blood they poured out all around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them."
17. Terror and dread fell upon all the people, for they said: "There is no truth or justice in them — they have broken the agreement and the oath they swore."
18. Bacchides withdrew from Jerusalem and camped at Beth-zaith. He had many of those who had deserted him seized and killed, and he threw some of the people into the great cistern.
19. He put the country in Alcimus's charge, leaving troops to support him, and then returned to the king.
20. Alcimus fought to maintain his hold on the high priesthood.
21. All who were disrupting their people gathered to him; they gained control of the land of Judah and inflicted great suffering on Israel.
22. Judas saw all the harm that Alcimus and his followers had done to the Israelites — harm worse than the Gentiles had done.
23. He went out into all the surrounding territory of Judea and took vengeance on the deserters, and they were prevented from going about in the country.
24. When Alcimus saw that Judas and his men were gaining in strength and that he could not hold out against them, he went back to the king and brought many charges against them.
25. The king sent Nicanor, one of his honored princes, a bitter enemy of Israel, with orders to destroy the people.
26. Nicanor came to Jerusalem with a large force and sent deceptive messages of peace to Judas and his brothers, saying:
27. "Let there be no battle between us. I will come with a few men so that we may meet one another in peace."
28. He came to Judas, and they greeted one another peaceably; but the enemy was ready to seize Judas.
29. When it became known to Judas that Nicanor had come to him with treachery, he became afraid and refused to meet him again.
30. When Nicanor realized that his plan had been found out, he advanced to meet Judas in battle near Capharsalama.
31. About five hundred of Nicanor's men fell, and the survivors fled to the city of David.
32. After these events Nicanor went up to Mount Zion; some of the priests from the sanctuary and some of the elders of the people came out to greet him peacefully
33. and to show him the burnt offering being offered on the king's behalf.
34. But he mocked them, derided them, defiled them, and spoke arrogantly.
35. In anger he swore an oath: "Unless Judas and his army are delivered into my hands, then as sure as I return safely, I will burn this house to the ground." He left in a violent rage.
36. The priests went back inside, stood before the altar and the temple, and wept, saying:
37. "You chose this house to bear your name — to be a house of prayer and supplication for your people.
38. Take vengeance on this man and his army; let them fall by the sword. Remember their blasphemies, and do not let them endure."
39. Nicanor left Jerusalem and camped at Beth-horon, where the Syrian army came to reinforce him.
40. Judas camped at Adasa with three thousand men. He prayed and said:
41. "When those envoys of the king spoke blasphemies, your angel went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand of them.
42. In the same way, crush this army before us today; let the rest know how viciously he has spoken against your sanctuary; and judge him according to his wickedness."
43. On the thirteenth day of the month of Adar the two armies met in battle; Nicanor's army was defeated, and Nicanor himself was the first to fall.
44. When his army saw that Nicanor had fallen, they threw down their weapons and fled.
45. The Judean forces pursued them a full day's journey from Adasa to Gazara, sounding the signal trumpets behind them.
46. Men came out of all the surrounding villages of Judea, and they outflanked the retreating enemy, driving them back on themselves; they all fell by the sword, and not one of them survived.
47. Then the Judeans collected the plunder and the spoils; they cut off Nicanor's head and his right arm, which he had stretched out in arrogance, and brought them and hung them up near Jerusalem.
48. The people rejoiced greatly and celebrated that day as a great festival.
49. They ordained that this day should be observed every year on the thirteenth of Adar.
50. And the land of Judah had rest for a little while.
